symptom: MDL could create a module and write its themesource SCSS but could not mark it a UI resources module nor place it in App Settings > Theme > module order; scripted setup had to stop for Studio Pro.
cause: Neither Projects$ModuleImpl.IsThemeModule nor Forms$WebUIProjectSettingsPart.ThemeModuleOrder (a list of Settings$ThemeModuleEntry {ModuleName}) had a statement, a model field or a write path.
file: mdl/backend/modelsdk/module_write.go (SetModuleUIResources), mdl/executor/cmd_module_settings.go, mdl/settingsoverlay/settingsoverlay.go (ThemeModuleOrder), mdl/backend/modelsdk/settings_read.go, mdl/executor/cmd_settings.go, validate_settings.go, validate.go, MDLSettings.g4 (list value)
fix: UIResources key on the module settings clause, written by a dedicated backend method; ThemeModuleOrder on ALTER SETTINGS WEBUI as a parenthesised list, overlaid onto the stored part reusing entries by module name; describe prints both; check refuses duplicates, unknown modules and lists on scalar keys.
insight: Measure the effect, not just acceptance: a probe that wrote the raw entries passed mx check, but only a deploy build with a marker class in themesource and a byte offset in theme.compiled.css showed the order actually drives compilation (first vs last), that unlisted modules keep a default place, and that the default (empty) order already compiles a user module last. Two storage gotchas: the part is Forms$WebUIProjectSettingsPart, not Settings$, and a hand-built $ID must be binary subtype 0 (bsonutil), or mx fails with \"Expected '$ID' as the first property … but got '$ID'\". A flag on the module unit must not ride UpdateModule, whose callers hold Name+ID only and would reset it on rename.
test: mdl/executor/theme_module_order_1286_test.go (parse, refusals, describe), mdl/settingsoverlay/theme_module_order_1286_test.go (stored entries kept by name)
